findings.reason: the rule must say the plan's section ids are compared through `_section_key`/`section_record_id`, with a dotted-id case, or the guard tests green and misses a section spelling the codebase explicitly supports (`reckon/_plan_html.py` section_id_candidates docstring, "the dotted one an author may have used (``s5.1``)").
findings.text: the producible-id set and the append refusal both take "the plan's section ids" as authored, but `_render_document` writes `_section_key(raw_id)` (reckon/evidence.py:70,349,372), so a plan section authored `id="s5.1"` renders as `id="s5-1"` (`_section_key("s5.1")` returns `"s5-1"`, verified in the repo's venv); for such a plan an unmarked `s5-1` section left by an earlier synthesis is classified as appended and carried, and an append anchored `s5-1` is not refused, which is exactly the case-3 stale-section and case-6 collision the plan exists to stop — the third and sixth cases cannot show it because `s9` and `s4` are identities where the authored and rendered spellings coincide

findings.reason: a worker taking the clause as a description of existing behaviour looks for a ledger read to extend, finds none, and can most cheaply drop that arm of the guard rather than add it.
findings.text: the refusal is placed in `_apply_evidence_appends` because it is "the half of the op that has the docs directory and reads the ledger", but that function (reckon/_store.py:1230–1275) reads no ledger and does not import `reckon.ledger`; `_store.py` imports it lazily only at line 4573, and the only plan read nearby is `_evidence_plan_title` (1177), reached only when the record file is missing — so both inputs the refusal needs (the plan's section ids and comment keys, the current ledger run sections) must be added, not extended

findings.reason: the ledger arm is the part that stops a future `section` key colliding with an anchor already published, and without a case or control the gate cannot show it fires, so the narrower guard ships as a pass.
findings.text: the deliverable requires the refusal to cover "every id `_section_key` makes of ... the current ledger runs' `section` keys", but the sixth case anchors `s4`, a plan section id, and no case anchors an id that only a ledger run renders; a refusal that checks plan sections and comment keys alone passes all eight cases and all eight controls
